title: Degreewise-injective ordinary etale support sequence
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow P$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a module sheaf $M$ put $H_A(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, where the map is the open adjunction unit. The canonical supported-sheaf isomorphism identifies this kernel with $i_*H_A(M)$, and its inclusion is the counit of $i_*\dashv H_A$. Let $I$ be a degreewise-injective K-injective cochain complex representing $L\in D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then
$$0\to i_*H_A(I)\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$$
is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes, natural in chain maps between such $I$. The complex $H_A(I)$ represents $Ri_A^!L$, the ordinary right adjoint of $i_*$, and $j_*j^*I$ represents $Rj_*j^*L$. The associated short-exact-sequence triangle, including its natural connecting morphism, realizes the counit/unit support triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. No injectivity after forgetting coefficient scalars is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing module-valued closed support adjunction and the upstream isomorphism closedUpperShriekCompLowerStarIso to identify its counit with the kernel inclusion of the open unit. Thus the composite of the two maps is zero. The open unit is split epic on an injective sheaf: the counit of extension by zero is monic, so injectivity extends the transpose of the open counit; the adjunction identities show the extension splits the open unit. This is the proved upstream isSplitEpi_upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_unit_app_of_injective. Transport the kernel fork through the support isomorphism and apply degreewise exactness of complexes.

source.place: Tags 09XQ and 0A45, supported kernel and injective support sequence; upstream ordinary-etale SupportedSections and Supports

proof.text: The exact extension-by-zero functor is left adjoint to open restriction. Hence its right adjoint preserves K-injective complexes, giving K-injectivity of j^*I directly, without identifying the etale site with a localized site or constructing another resolution.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, right adjoints of exact functors preserve K-injectives; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FI

proof.text: Apply the derived unit and counit factorization identities to the homotopy-category adjunctions, then the localization comparison isomorphisms and the right-derived-unit isomorphisms at K-injective complexes. These give compatibility of the specified third comparison with the actual derived open unit, and compatibility of the specified first comparison with the derived closed counit. For the latter also use the counit-compatible uniqueness isomorphism to the recorded right adjoint of closed direct image. Naturality transports both squares along any representing isomorphism QI ≅ L. The private helpers prove all this comparison algebra, with no new mathematical assumption.

source.place: Tags 070K and 08BJ; derived adjunction and the canonical comparison on K-injectives

proof.text: Take the natural boundary and distinguished counit/unit triangle already provided by lem-exc-closed-support-triangle. The support SES gives another distinguished triangle. The first two comparison isomorphisms extend to an isomorphism of triangles by the triangulated axiom. Its third component must equal the specified open comparison: the relevant Hom(i_*Ri^!L[1], Rj_*j^*L) is zero by the open adjunction, commutation with shifts, and vanishing of j^*i_* for disjoint ranges. Cancel the second arrow of the SES triangle using this zero Hom group. This proves all three prescribed components simultaneously for arbitrary L and e.

proof.text: The termwise counit and unit are natural, so they give etaleSupportSequenceMap for every chain map. Apply DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ_naturality to this short-complex morphism. This is exactly the asserted boundary naturality, with the canonical SES sign.
